title: deadline-aware-nms: bounded candidate admission for deadline-critical NMS-based object detection
description:
Reference implementation of the defense, attack objective and deadline metrics from the paper Deadline-Aware Hardening of Real-Time Object Detection Against Candidate-Inflation Latency Attacks.

An NMS-based detector performs an amount of work set by the number of candidates surviving its confidence threshold, and that number is chosen by the input. A candidate-inflation attack drives it far outside its clean range and the application deadline is what pays. Admitting at most K candidates to suppression bounds the pairwise comparisons an attacker can provoke, without retraining or weight modification, at the exported runtime boundary.

Contents: the admission cap with membership defined lexicographically so that a tied cutoff is deterministic; greedy IoU suppression as the serving path runs it, visiting candidates in the same (score, index) order as admission, with optional class-aware comparison and an output limit, so that the conditions under which the cap leaves the output unchanged can be checked; the differentiable candidate-count surrogate and its projected-gradient recurrence; tail quantile and deadline-miss ratio; a cluster-level Clopper–Pearson bound on the deadline-exceedance probability with a PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE verdict; and deadline-calibrated selection of K by fixed-sequence testing. A runnable demonstration on synthetic candidates needs no dataset, weights or GPU.
